newsitem.title: UK: UK's Pearson acquires US publisher Putnam Berkley.
newsitem.headline: UK's Pearson acquires US publisher Putnam Berkley.

text.p: British media group Pearson Plc said on Tuesday that its Penguin books unit had acquired Putnam Berkley, a leading U.S. publisher of popular fiction, from MCA INC for 336 million dollars.
It said the acquisition would be earnings enhancing from the first year of ownership.

The acquisition will make Penguin the second largest English language trade book publisher in the world and the third largest in the United States. Putnam Berkley's authors include Tom Clancy, Patricia Cornwell, Dick Francis and Kurt Vonnegut.
"This is a terrific acquisition for Penguin," said Michael Lynton, who takes over as chairman and chief executive of Penguin Group at the end of the year.
"The two businesses complement each other extremely well in terms of both authors and people and will create great opportunities for the future. It is a marvellous way to start at Penguin," he added.
MCA Inc is owned 80 percent by Seagram Company Limited and 20 percent by Matsushita of Japan.
